title: Late deliveries point to a dispatch problem at East

report.originalQuestion: Why are more orders arriving late, and what should we fix first?

metricDefinitions.label: week
metricDefinitions.definition: Monday of original promised-delivery week, not the exact exposure date.

metricDefinitions.label: orders
metricDefinitions.definition: Every non-canceled domestic standard-delivery order placed by 16:00 local warehouse time and eligible for same-day dispatch, with an original promised date in the reporting window, grouped by the Monday of that promised-delivery week. Late means delivered after the original promise, or still undelivered after that date at the August 20 cutoff. The sample includes all eligible orders; all happen to have a final delivery scan by the cutoff, so none were excluded as undelivered. Express, pickup, and split shipments are outside scope. Promise timestamps and logging definitions are unchanged. Orders placed after 16:00 are explicitly outside this case, not assumed to be zero.

metricDefinitions.label: lateOrders
metricDefinitions.definition: Orders delivered after the original promise. All have final scans by August 20.

metricDefinitions.label: lateRate
metricDefinitions.definition: lateOrders / orders, displayed as a percentage.

metricDefinitions.label: context
metricDefinitions.definition: OPS-17 supplies the schedule change. Timing does not establish its causal effect.

evidenceFlow.title: Synthetic evidence and scope
evidenceFlow.detail: No real company, live query, or interview is represented. Promise timestamps and logging definitions are unchanged. Orders placed after 16:00 are explicitly outside this case, not assumed to be zero.

evidenceFlow.title: OPS-17
evidenceFlow.detail: 2026-07-20 · East collection time changed without a packing-wave change. The East weekday collection moved from 18:00 to 16:30 local time on July 20. The afternoon packing wave still starts at 16:45. Checkout still accepts eligible orders for the same dispatch day until 16:00. West collection and packing schedules are unchanged. The cohort chart places the event in the week beginning July 20; its rates group orders by promised delivery week, not the exact day they encountered the change.

evidenceFlow.title: QA-1
evidenceFlow.detail: 2026-08-20 · Order counts, promise dates, and dispatch classifications reconcile. Weekly, warehouse, placement-time, and failure-stage cuts reconcile to 16,000 baseline orders with 640 late and 20,000 recent orders with 1,960 late. Failure-stage buckets apply only to late-delivered orders and are mutually exclusive: missed the planned dispatch collection, or handed off by that collection and delivered late. A late order that misses dispatch remains in that first bucket even if the carrier also delays it. The classification locates a failure stage; it does not assign responsibility or prove that avoiding that failure would prevent late delivery. All counts in this report are fictional, authored for this example. Order time means placement time in each warehouse’s local timezone (East: America/New_York; West: America/Los_Angeles). The latest planned dispatch collection that could meet each original customer promise determines the stage deadline. The warehouse mix calculation first changes warehouse rates at baseline shares, then changes shares at recent rates. It is an order-dependent accounting split, not causal attribution. All cuts use orders placed by 16:00 local warehouse time and eligible for same-day dispatch. After-cutoff orders are outside the question tested by this packet.

metricDefinitions.label: stage
metricDefinitions.definition: Mutually exclusive first failure: missed planned dispatch, or handed off on time but delivered late. Not responsibility or causal attribution.

metricDefinitions.label: expectedAtCurrentVolume
metricDefinitions.definition: Baseline stage count × recent orders / baseline orders.

metricDefinitions.label: extraLateOrders
metricDefinitions.definition: Volume: added orders × baseline late rate. Other stages: recent late orders minus expectedAtCurrentVolume. All three sum to 1320 additional late orders.

evidenceFlow.detail: 2026-08-18 · An extra 18:00 collection costs $450 per weekday. evidenceFlow.title: CX-6
evidenceFlow.detail: 2026-08-19 · Late deliveries trigger an $8 service credit. The fictional service policy issued one $8 credit per late order in both periods: $5,120 for 640 baseline late orders and $15,680 for 1,960 recent late orders. Support staff describe repeat where-is-my-order contacts, but the packet has no validated handling-cost or repeat-purchase estimate. Credits are not the full customer or economic impact.
